claim.text: In sparse non-Hermitian synaptic matrices, transient dynamics and effective memory capacity are governed primarily by the non-normality of the operator (pseudospectrum / Kreiss constant / numerical radius), not by the eigenvalue distribution: two ensembles with an identical eigenvalue spectrum but different sparsity-induced non-normality will show systematically different transient amplification and memory.

d8_handling.public_attestation: No source PDF/full text was ingested into the duel context; only bibliographic/search-result metadata and abstracts informed topic selection.

references.ref: Ansari, M. G., & Shukla, P. (2026). On the synaptic matrix eigenvalues of sparsely connected neural networks (arXiv:2606.00326). arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00326
references.note: Seed paper the duel was built on: characterises the eigenvalue spectrum of sparse synaptic matrices and links sparsity type to stability and transients through the spectrum.

references.ref: Ganguli, S., Huh, D., & Sompolinsky, H. (2008). Memory traces in dynamical systems. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 105(48), 18970–18975. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0804451105
references.note: Supporting: memory and non-normal amplification in linear neural dynamics; anchor for the memory half of the thesis.

references.ref: Trefethen, L. N., & Embree, M. (2005). Spectra and pseudospectra: The behavior of nonnormal matrices and operators. Princeton University Press.
references.note: Supporting: pseudospectra and the Kreiss matrix theorem; formal basis for using the Kreiss constant as the transient yardstick.
